sections.skill: Spot truncated output and formatting errors

questions.prompt: In this fictional example, what problem does the response show?

choices.text: It was cut off before finishing
It was formatted as a numbered list

questions.correct_answer: It was cut off before finishing
questions.intro: Two output problems are easy to miss. TRUNCATION: the answer stops partway because it hit a length limit, so a list ends at item 7 of 10, a table loses its last rows, or code stops mid-line. Signs include a sentence that ends abruptly, a list that skips its promised count, or a missing conclusion. FORMATTING ERRORS: broken tables, numbering that restarts, merged columns, or symbols that display wrongly after copying. Before using output, check that it is COMPLETE (does it reach the end?) and that its format survived the trip to where you will use it.

sections.skill: Count what was promised versus what arrived

questions.prompt: You asked for 12 monthly rows and see 9. What is wrong?

choices.text: Nothing, because 9 rows is close enough to a full year for most purposes
The months are in the wrong order

questions.intro: A simple check catches most truncation: COUNT. If you asked for 10 items, count the items. If a table should have one row per month, count 12 rows. If an outline promised 5 sections, find all 5. Also read the LAST line: it should be a complete sentence or a clear ending. Example: you asked for 8 tips and see tips 1-6, with tip 6 ending "and then you can" with no ending. Count fails (6 of 8) and the last line is cut off.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Handle quiet truncation and broken formats

questions.prompt: A summary of a 6-section report ends after section 5 but sounds finished. What is the risk?
questions.intro: Truncation is especially risky when it is quiet: a summary that stops before the last section may look complete, and a cut-off code file may still run but skip the final steps. Ask for long output in parts ("items 1 to 5, then 6 to 10"), and count what you asked for. Formatting can break when you paste between apps: a table may become one long line, or bullet symbols may turn into odd characters. Check the final destination, not just the chat window.

questions.prompt: Cut-off code still runs without an error. Why might it be a problem?

choices.text: Because code that runs without an error is always completely correct and complete
It may skip the final steps

questions.correct_answer: It may skip the final steps
